SMTO-CFG-0018 — This conversation was deleted or can't be found

GUID: 385db5fb-5803-4fea-a590-24f677f20c17
Slug: composer-conversation-missing
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't find the conversation you're working in. It may have been deleted on another device or removed by automatic cleanup. Your last change or message wasn't saved to it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If your message is still in the message box, copy it somewhere safe first. The conversation it was meant for is gone, so you'll need to send it again elsewhere.
  2. Open the Conversations pane and look for the conversation, using Search conversations… if needed. If it's still listed, opening it from the list loads it fresh; if it's missing, it was deleted.
  3. If it's gone, select New chat, paste your message and send it. A new conversation gives your message a valid place to run.

What success looks like

  • Your message appears in a conversation listed in the Conversations pane and a task starts.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages SMTO, especially if the conversation vanished without anyone deleting it. They can check Settings › Data › Auto-purge to see whether automatic cleanup removed it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The composer profile read/update or task admission could not find the conversation ID in the conversation store, so the request was refused before anything was written.

What this means

  • Composer read/write/admission cannot find the selected conversation record in the joined or owned conversation store. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • Composer read/write/admission cannot find the selected conversation record in the joined or owned conversation store.

How to diagnose it

  • Refresh conversation existence and exact ID at the same settings/admission boundary.

How to fix it

  • Confirm whether the conversation ID still exists in the conversations store; it may have been deleted or auto-purged (Settings › Data › Auto-purge). Clients should refresh the conversation list and open an existing conversation or create a new one instead of resubmitting to the removed ID.
  • Open an existing conversation or start a new one.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended existing conversation owns the profile being read or edited.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
